title: Annotatio IV §.VII: Tertullian Contra Marcionem — Hoc est corpus meum = figure of my body
pass_a_gloss: But, he says, Christ made that bread which He had taken and distributed to the Disciples His Body, saying: This is my body, i.e. THE FIGURE OF MY BODY; But it would not have been a Figure unless it had BEEN A BODY OF TRUTH: For an empty thing, as a phantasm is, cannot take a figure. Against Marcion book 4 ch. 40.
pass_b_english: Contra Marcionem 4.40: Christ made the bread taken and given to the disciples His Body by saying ‘This is my body’ — that is, the FIGURE OF MY BODY.
It would not be a figure unless it were a BODY OF TRUTH: an empty phantasm cannot take a figure.
source_text: At inquit, Christus acceptum panem & distributum Discipulis, Corpus suum illum fecit, dicendo: Hoc est corpus meum, i. e. FIGURA CORPORIS MEI; Figura verò non fuisset, nisi VERITATIS FUISSET CORPUS: Res enim vacua, ut est phantasma, figuram capere non potest. Contra Marcionem lib. 4. c. 40.
